1.topic: Àkókò ìṣe àti gbólóhùn àyọkúrò (Tense, negation and linking words in sentences)
1.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. use the markers ń, ti and yóò (or máa) to show an action in progress, a completed action and a future action;
2. turn a positive sentence into a negative one with kò, ò, ò ní and ò tíì;
3. use linking words (nítorí náà, kí, tí) to make longer sentences.

## Materials

Three sentence strips for each tense, cards with ń, ti and yóò, pictures of a child before, during and after a meal, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Show the three pictures. Ask pupils in Yoruba: Kí ni ọmọ náà ń ṣe? (What is the child doing?) Take answers, then ask what he did before and what he will do next.

## Development

1. Revise the simple, compound and complex sentences from JSS1.
2. Teach the three time markers using one verb: Mo ń jẹun (I am eating). Mo ti jẹun (I have eaten). Màá jẹun (I will eat).
3. Teach the negatives: Mi ò jẹun (I do not or did not eat). Mi ò tíì jẹun (I have not eaten yet). Mi ò ní jẹun (I will not eat). Stress the order: the negative word comes before the verb, and the subject pronoun takes its negative form (mi ò, kò, a kò, ẹ kò, wọn kò).
4. Teach the relative clause with tí: Ìwé tí mo kà dára (The book that I read is good). Ọmọ tí ó ń kàwé ni Ayọ̀.
5. Teach kí for purpose: Mo kàwé kí n lè yege (I read so that I can pass), and nítorí náà (therefore): Òjò ń rọ̀, nítorí náà a kò lọ ṣeré.
6. Pupils write sentences from pictures and exchange for checking.

## Class activity

Tense line: pupils stand in three lines (past, now, future). The teacher gives a verb and each line says the sentence in its tense.

## Evaluation

1. Say "I am eating" and "I have eaten" in Yoruba.
2. Make "Mo lọ sí ọjà" negative.
3. Join the two ideas with nítorí náà: Òjò ń rọ̀. A kò lọ ṣeré.

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Àkókò ìṣe àti gbólóhùn àyọkúrò

Bí a bá fẹ́ sọ ohun tí a ń ṣe, tí a ti ṣe tàbí tí a óò ṣe, a máa ń lo àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ kékeré kan pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe.

## Àwọn àmì àkókò

| Àmì | Ìtumọ̀ | Àpẹẹrẹ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ń | iṣẹ́ tí ń lọ lọ́wọ́ | Mo ń jẹun. (I am eating.) |
| ti | iṣẹ́ tí ó ti parí | Mo ti jẹun. (I have eaten.) |
| yóò / máa | iṣẹ́ ọjọ́ iwájú | Màá jẹun. (I will eat.) |

Pẹ̀lú orúkọ olùṣe iṣẹ́, a kì í tún pe arọ́pò-orúkọ: **Ọmọ náà ń jẹun**, kì í ṣe "Ọmọ náà ó ń jẹun".

## Gbólóhùn àyọkúrò (negative)

Láti sọ pé a kò ṣe nǹkan, a máa ń lo **kò** tàbí **ò**.

| Rere | Àyọkúrò |
| --- | --- |
| Mo jẹun. | Mi ò jẹun. |
| Ó lọ sí ọjà. | Kò lọ sí ọjà. |
| A jẹ iṣu. | A kò jẹ iṣu. |
| Mo ti jẹun. | Mi ò tíì jẹun. |
| Màá jẹun. | Mi ò ní jẹun. |

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí:

- "Mi ò" ni a máa ń lò fún "èmi". A kì í sọ "Mo kò".
- Fún ọjọ́ iwájú, a máa ń fi **ní** kún un: Mi ò **ní** jẹun.
- Fún "kò tíì" (not yet), a máa ń lo **tíì**: Mi ò **tíì** jẹun.

## Gbólóhùn pẹ̀lú "tí"

"Tí" so orúkọ mọ́ gbólóhùn tí ó ṣàlàyé rẹ̀.

- Ìwé **tí** mo kà dára. (The book that I read is good.)
- Ọmọ **tí** ó ń kàwé ni Ayọ̀. (The child who is reading is Ayọ̀.)

## Ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀

- **Nítorí náà** túmọ̀ sí "therefore": Òjò ń rọ̀, nítorí náà a kò lọ ṣeré.
- **Kí** fi ète hàn: Mo kàwé kí n lè yege. (I read so that I can pass.)
- **Ṣùgbọ́n** túmọ̀ sí "but".

## Àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

1. "Mo yóò jẹun lánàá." Lánàá jẹ́ àná, nítorí náà a kò lè lo yóò.
2. "Mo kò lọ." Ó yẹ kí a sọ pé "Mi ò lọ."
3. "Ọmọ náà ó ń jẹun." Ó yẹ kí a sọ pé "Ọmọ náà ń jẹun."

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Àmì àkókò àti àyọkúrò gbọdọ̀ bá ìgbà tí iṣẹ́ ṣẹlẹ̀ mu. Kọ gbogbo àmì ohùn.

2.topic: Àwọn ẹ̀yà ọ̀rọ̀: arọ́pò-orúkọ àbọ̀ àti oní-nǹkan, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe àti ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe (Parts of speech in use)
2.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. use the object pronouns (mi, ọ, i or rẹ̀, wa, yín, wọn) after a verb;
2. use the possessive forms (mi, rẹ, rẹ̀, wa, yín, wọn) after a noun;
3. pick out nouns, pronouns, verbs and adjectives in a longer sentence.

## Materials

A chart of the subject pronouns, object pronouns and possessive forms; sentence strips cut into words; coloured chalk (one colour for each part of speech).

## Starter (5 minutes)

Write on the board: Mo rí Ayọ̀. Ayọ̀ rí mi. Ask: what happened to mo? Lead pupils to see that the pronoun changes form when it comes after the verb.

## Development

1. Revise JSS1: orúkọ, arọ́pò-orúkọ, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe, ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe.
2. Subject pronouns come before the verb: mo, o, ó, a, ẹ, wọ́n. Object pronouns come after the verb: Ó rí mi (he saw me). Mo rí ọ (I saw you). Mo rí i (I saw him or her). Ó rí wa (he saw us). Mo rí yín (I saw you, plural or respect). Mo rí wọn (I saw them).
3. Possessive forms come after the noun: ìwé mi (my book), ìwé rẹ (your book), ìwé rẹ̀ (his or her book), ìwé wa (our book), ìwé yín (your book, plural), ìwé wọn (their book).
4. Practise with word strips. Pupils change a sentence from subject to object form: Mo rí wọn becomes Wọ́n rí mi.
5. Analyse a longer sentence together: "Ọmọ kékeré náà rí ajá dúdú, ó sì sá lọ." Colour each word: nouns in one colour, adjectives in another, verbs in a third and the pronoun in a fourth. Ask what the pronoun ó stands for.
6. Remind pupils that the adjective follows its noun (ajá dúdú).

## Class activity

Pupils get ten sentence strips. In pairs they colour each word by part of speech, then swap with another pair to check.

## Evaluation

1. Write "he saw me" in Yoruba.
2. Write "our book" in Yoruba.
3. Name two adjectives from the sentence "Ọmọ kékeré náà rí ajá dúdú".

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

# Arọ́pò-orúkọ àbọ̀ àti ti oní-nǹkan

Ní JSS1, a kọ́ nípa orúkọ, arọ́pò-orúkọ, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe àti ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe. Lónìí, a ó wo bí arọ́pò-orúkọ ṣe ń yí fọ́ọ̀mù padà ní ibi tí ó wà nínú gbólóhùn.

## Arọ́pò-orúkọ olùṣe iṣẹ́ (subject)

Wọ́n máa ń wà ṣáájú ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe: **mo, o, ó, a, ẹ, wọ́n**.

- Mo rí Ayọ̀.
- Ó ń kàwé.
- Wọ́n ń ṣeré.

## Arọ́pò-orúkọ àbọ̀ (object)

Wọ́n máa ń wà lẹ́yìn ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe: **mi, ọ, i (tàbí rẹ̀), wa, yín, wọn**.

| Olùṣe | Àbọ̀ | Àpẹẹrẹ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mo | mi | Ayọ̀ rí **mi**. |
| o | ọ | Mo rí **ọ**. |
| ó | i | Mo rí **i**. |
| a | wa | Ó rí **wa**. |
| ẹ | yín | Mo rí **yín**. |
| wọ́n | wọn | Mo rí **wọn**. |

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé "wọ́n" (olùṣe) ní ohùn òkè, ṣùgbọ́n "wọn" (àbọ̀) kò ní àmì.

## Arọ́pò-orúkọ oní-nǹkan (possessive)

Wọ́n máa ń wà lẹ́yìn orúkọ.

- ìwé **mi** (my book)
- ìwé **rẹ** (your book)
- ìwé **rẹ̀** (his or her book)
- ìwé **wa** (our book)
- ìwé **yín** (your book, plural or respect)
- ìwé **wọn** (their book)

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ìwé wa nìyí. (This is our book.)

## Pípín ọ̀rọ̀ nínú gbólóhùn gígùn

Wo gbólóhùn yìí: **Ọmọ kékeré náà rí ajá dúdú, ó sì sá lọ.**

| Ẹ̀yà ọ̀rọ̀ | Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| Orúkọ | ọmọ, ajá |
| Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe | kékeré, dúdú |
| Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe | rí, sá lọ |
| Arọ́pò-orúkọ | ó (ó dúró fún ọmọ) |

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe ń tẹ̀lé orúkọ rẹ̀: ọmọ kékeré, ajá dúdú.

## Ìmọ̀ràn fún ìdánrawò

1. Wá ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe kọ́kọ́.
2. Wá ẹni tí ó ṣe iṣẹ́ náà: ó jẹ́ orúkọ tàbí arọ́pò-orúkọ olùṣe.
3. Wá ẹni tí iṣẹ́ náà dé bá: ó jẹ́ àbọ̀.
4. Wá àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń ṣàpèjúwe orúkọ.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Arọ́pò-orúkọ ń yí fọ́ọ̀mù padà gẹ́gẹ́ bí ibi tí ó wà nínú gbólóhùn. Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe ń tẹ̀lé orúkọ.

cards.back: Mo jẹ́ olùṣe (subject); mi jẹ́ àbọ̀ àti oní-nǹkan (me, my).

Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń tẹ̀lé orúkọ láti ṣàpèjúwe rẹ̀ (adjective).
Arọ́pò-orúkọ tí ó wà lẹ́yìn ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe (object pronoun).

3.topic: Nọ́ńbà tó tóbi, déètì àti àkókò (Larger numbers, dates and time)
3.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. count and write the numbers eleven to twenty, and thirty, forty, fifty and one hundred in Yoruba;
2. write a date using the day, the ordinal number and the month;
3. tell the time on the hour and the half hour and name the part of the day.

## Materials

A number line from 1 to 20 on the wall, a calendar, a clock with movable hands, cards for the ordinals (kìíní, kejì, kẹta, kẹrin, karùn-ún, kẹfà, keje, kẹjọ, kẹsàn-án, kẹwàá), chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Revise JSS1: pupils count from one to ten, say the days and the months. Then ask the date of Nigeria's independence (the first of October) and write it as Ọjọ́ kìíní oṣù Ọ̀wàrà.

## Development

1. Teach the numbers eleven to twenty: mọ́kànlá, méjìlá, mẹ́tàlá, mẹ́rìnlá, mẹ́ẹ̀dógún, mẹ́rìndínlógún, mẹ́tàdínlógún, méjìdínlógún, mọ́kàndínlógún, ogún. Pupils chant them with the number line. Note that the form changes when the number is used with a noun, as in ọmọ méjìlá.
2. Teach the tens: ogún (20), ọgbọ̀n (30), ogójì (40), àádọ́ta (50), ọgọ́rùn-ún (100).
3. Teach the ordinals: kìíní, kejì, kẹta, kẹrin, karùn-ún, kẹfà, keje, kẹjọ, kẹsàn-án, kẹwàá. Use them with ọjọ́: ọjọ́ kẹta.
4. Teach the date pattern: Ọjọ́ [ordinal] oṣù [month], as in Ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà. Warn against reversing it as in English.
5. Teach the half hour: aago méjì àbọ̀ (half past two). Practise with the clock: Aago mélòó ni? Aago mẹ́ta àbọ̀ ni.
6. Pupils write a short notice giving a day, date, time and place.

## Class activity

Pupils each get a card with a date and time and write a sentence announcing it. They read out loud and the class corrects the tone marks.

## Evaluation

1. Write twelve and twenty in Yoruba.
2. Write "the third of November".
3. What time is it when the clock shows half past four?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Nọ́ńbà, déètì àti àkókò

## Nọ́ńbà mọ́kànlá sí ogún

| Nọ́ńbà | Yorùbá |
| --- | --- |
| 11 | mọ́kànlá |
| 12 | méjìlá |
| 13 | mẹ́tàlá |
| 14 | mẹ́rìnlá |
| 15 | mẹ́ẹ̀dógún |
| 16 | mẹ́rìndínlógún |
| 17 | mẹ́tàdínlógún |
| 18 | méjìdínlógún |
| 19 | mọ́kàndínlógún |
| 20 | ogún |

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ọmọ méjìlá wà nínú kíláàsì. Mo ní ìwé mẹ́ẹ̀dógún.

## Àwọn nọ́ńbà mìíràn

- 30: ọgbọ̀n
- 40: ogójì
- 50: àádọ́ta
- 100: ọgọ́rùn-ún

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ọgọ́rùn-ún náírà ni. Ogún ọmọ ni ó wà níbẹ̀.

## Nọ́ńbà ìtẹ̀lé (ordinals)

kìíní (first), kejì (second), kẹta (third), kẹrin (fourth), karùn-ún (fifth), kẹfà (sixth), keje (seventh), kẹjọ (eighth), kẹsàn-án (ninth), kẹwàá (tenth).

A máa ń lò wọ́n pẹ̀lú **ọjọ́** láti sọ ọjọ́ oṣù: **ọjọ́ kẹta** (the third day).

## Bí a ṣe ń kọ déètì

Ìlànà: **Ọjọ́ + nọ́ńbà ìtẹ̀lé + oṣù + orúkọ oṣù**

- Ọjọ́ kìíní oṣù Ọ̀wàrà (1 October)
- Ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà (10 October)
- Ọjọ́ kẹta oṣù Bélú (3 November)

Ẹ ṣọ́ra: Nínú Gẹ̀ẹ́sì, a lè sọ pé "October 10". Ní Yorùbá, ọjọ́ ni a kọ́kọ́ sọ, lẹ́yìn náà oṣù.

Àpẹẹrẹ pẹ̀lú ọjọ́ ọ̀sẹ̀: Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà.

## Àkókò

Aago mélòó ni?

- Aago méjì ni. (It is two o'clock.)
- Aago méjì àbọ̀ ni. (It is half past two.)
- Aago mẹ́jọ àárọ̀ ni. (It is eight in the morning.)
- Aago mẹ́ta ọ̀sán ni. (It is three in the afternoon.)

**Àbọ̀** túmọ̀ sí "half".

## Ìkéde kékeré

Ìkéde ṣe pàtàkì nínú ilé ìwé. Ó gbọdọ̀ sọ ọjọ́, déètì, àkókò àti ibi.

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ayẹyẹ ilé ìwé wa yóò wáyé ní Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà, ní aago mẹ́wàá àárọ̀, ní gbọ̀ngàn ilé ìwé.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Kọ ọjọ́ kí o tó kọ oṣù. Kọ àmì ohùn gbogbo nọ́ńbà.

4.topic: Àmì ohùn àti àwọn àmì ìkọ̀wé Yorùbá (Tone marks and writing conventions)
4.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. place tone marks and under-dots correctly on Yoruba words, including letters that carry both (ẹ́, ẹ̀, ọ́, ọ̀);
2. explain how the meaning of a word changes when the tone mark changes;
3. correct a sentence written without marks.

## Materials

Word cards for the minimal pairs (ìyá and ìyà, ilé and ilẹ̀, ẹgbẹ́ and ẹ̀gbẹ́), a large sentence on the board without marks, coloured chalk for marks, slates.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Write on the board: Iya mi ra ile. Ask three pupils to read it aloud and to say what they understand. Several readings are possible. Tell the class that the marks decide the meaning.

## Development

1. Revise the three tones and the three under-dotted letters. Show how a letter with an under-dot receives the tone mark above it: ẹ, ẹ́, ẹ̀; ọ, ọ́, ọ̀.
2. Teach the minimal pairs with a hand gesture for each tone: ìyá (mother) and ìyà (suffering); ilé (house) and ilẹ̀ (ground); ẹgbẹ́ (group) and ẹ̀gbẹ́ (side); ọkọ (husband), ọkọ̀ (vehicle), ọkọ́ (hoe).
3. Teach the rules for writing: capital letters keep their marks (Ìbàdàn, Ẹ káàárọ̀); the mid tone is not marked; the high mark on a syllabic nasal is written ń (Mo ń lọ).
4. Show the sentence on the board and add marks together: Ìyá mi ra ilé ní ẹ̀gbẹ́ ọjà. Show how Ìyà mi ra ilé would mean something different.
5. Pupils copy five words and mark them. Walk around and check.
6. Pupils write a pair of sentences, one with each word of a minimal pair.

## Class activity

Mark detective. Give each group a short paragraph without marks. They add the marks and read it aloud. The teacher reads the correct version and each group scores itself.

## Evaluation

1. What is the difference between ìyá and ìyà?
2. Mark the word "egbe" so that it means "side".
3. Why must we write tone marks?

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Àmì ohùn àti àwọn ìlànà kíkọ ọ̀rọ̀
reading.content:
# Àmì ohùn àti àwọn ìlànà kíkọ ọ̀rọ̀

Èdè Yorùbá jẹ́ èdè oníhùn. Ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ kan lè yí padà bí ohùn rẹ̀ bá yàtọ̀. Nítorí náà, a gbọdọ̀ kọ àmì ohùn àti ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ dáadáa.

## Àmì mẹ́ta

- Ohùn òkè: ´ (á)
- Ohùn ìsàlẹ̀: ` (à)
- Ohùn àárín: kò ní àmì (a)

## Lẹ́tà tí ó ní ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ àti àmì ohùn

Lẹ́tà ẹ, ọ àti ṣ ní ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀. Bí ẹ tàbí ọ bá ní ohùn òkè tàbí ìsàlẹ̀, a kọ àmì ohùn sí òkè lẹ́tà náà.

- ẹ, ẹ́, ẹ̀
- ọ, ọ́, ọ̀

Àpẹẹrẹ: ọ̀rẹ́ (friend), ẹ̀gbọ́n (elder brother or sister), ọjà (market).

## Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí àmì ohùn ṣe ìyàtọ̀ wọn

| Ọ̀rọ̀ méjì | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| ìyá / ìyà | mother / suffering |
| ilé / ilẹ̀ | house / ground, land |
| ẹgbẹ́ / ẹ̀gbẹ́ | group / side |
| ọkọ / ọkọ̀ / ọkọ́ | husband / vehicle / hoe |
| owó / ọwọ́ | money / hand |

Ẹ wo ìyàtọ̀ nínú gbólóhùn méjì wọ̀nyí:

- **Ìyá** mi ra ilé. (My mother bought a house.)
- **Ìyà** mi ra ilé. (My suffering bought a house. Kò ní ìtumọ̀ rere.)

## Àwọn ìlànà kíkọ

1. A kọ àmì ohùn sórí lẹ́tà ńlá pẹ̀lú: **Ìbàdàn**, **Ẹ káàárọ̀**.
2. A kì í kọ àmì sí ohùn àárín.
3. Bí fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì kan bá gùn, a kọ àmì ohùn rẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan: **káàárọ̀**.
4. Nínú **Mo ń lọ**, "ń" ni àmì iṣẹ́ tí ń lọ lọ́wọ́. A kọ ọ́ pẹ̀lú àmì ohùn òkè.
5. Ọ̀rọ̀ tí kò ní àmì lè ní ìtumọ̀ ju ọ̀kan lọ.

## Bí a ṣe ń ṣàtúnṣe gbólóhùn tí kò ní àmì

Gbólóhùn tí kò ní àmì: Iya mi ra ile ni egbe oja.

1. Ka gbólóhùn náà ní ohùn gíga, kí o gbọ́ ohùn tí ó tọ́.
2. Fi ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ sí ibi tí ó yẹ: ẹgbẹ́, ọjà.
3. Fi àmì ohùn sí ọ̀rọ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan.
4. Gbólóhùn tí a tún ṣe: **Ìyá mi ra ilé ní ẹ̀gbẹ́ ọjà.**

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Àmì ohùn jẹ́ ara ọ̀rọ̀. Bí a bá kọ ọ̀rọ̀ láìsí rẹ̀, ìtumọ̀ lè yí padà.

5.topic: Kíkà ọ̀rọ̀ Yorùbá sókè (Reading Yoruba aloud)
5.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. read a short Yoruba passage aloud, pronouncing the words with the correct tones;
2. pause correctly at commas and full stops and raise or lower the voice for questions and exclamations;
3. answer simple questions on what they have read.

## Materials

A short passage on a chart (see the reading), a pointer, a recording device if one is available, a timer, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

The teacher reads one sentence twice: once very fast without pauses and once at a good pace with the correct tones. Ask pupils which reading is easier to understand and why.

## Development

1. Read the passage aloud once while pupils listen with books closed. Then read it again with books open and pupils follow with a finger.
2. Teach the four habits of a good reader: say each word with its tones, pause briefly at a comma and longer at a full stop, keep a steady pace, and let the voice show feeling (a rise for a question, a firmer voice for an exclamation).
3. Practise in chorus: pupils echo the teacher one sentence at a time.
4. Practise in pairs: one pupil reads a paragraph, the other listens and notes one word with a wrong tone. Swap.
5. Individual reading: three or four pupils read a paragraph to the class. The class says one thing done well and one thing to improve.
6. Ask the comprehension questions in Yoruba: Ọjọ́ wo ni ìyá àti ọmọ lọ sí ọjà? Kí ni ìyá ra? Kí ló dé tí wọ́n fi dúró nínú ilé ìtajà?

## Class activity

Reading circle. In groups of four, each pupil reads one sentence in turn around the circle. If a pupil mispronounces a word, the group corrects it before moving on.

## Evaluation

1. How long should you pause at a comma?
2. What do you do with your voice when you read a question?
3. Read the first two sentences of the passage with the correct tones.

## Assignment

Quiz on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ọjọ́ kan ní ọjà Bódìjà
reading.content:
# Ọjọ́ kan ní ọjà Bódìjà

Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta ni. Ìyá mi gbé mi lọ sí ọjà Bódìjà. Ọjà náà tóbi gan-an, àwọn ènìyàn sì pọ̀ níbẹ̀. Àwọn obìnrin ń tà tòmátì, ata, iṣu àti ẹja.

Ìyá mi ra iṣu méjì, ó sì ra ata díẹ̀. Mo rí ọmọbìnrin kan tí ó ń tà omi. Mo ra omi kan, mo sì mu ún.

Nígbà tí a fẹ́ padà sílé, òjò bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí rọ̀. A sá wọ ilé ìtajà kan, a sì dúró títí tí òjò fi dá. Mo ní inú dídùn nítorí mo kọ́ ohun púpọ̀ ní ọjà.

## Bí a ṣe ń ka ìwé sókè

Kíkà sókè yàtọ̀ sí kíkà nínú ọkàn. Akàwé rere ń ṣe nǹkan wọ̀nyí:

1. **Ó ń pe ọ̀rọ̀ pẹ̀lú ohùn tí ó tọ́.** Ìyá, ọjà, iṣu, ata, tòmátì: kí ohùn òkè, ìsàlẹ̀ àti àárín hàn kedere.
2. **Ó ń dúró níbi tí ó yẹ.** Ó dúró díẹ̀ ní ibi kọ́mà (,) àti pẹ́ díẹ̀ jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ ní ibi ojú-ìdúró (.).
3. **Kì í kà yára jù.** Bí a bá yára jù, àwọn olùgbọ́ kò ní gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ náà dáadáa.
4. **Ó ń fi ìmọ̀lára hàn.** Fún ìbéèrè, ohùn máa ń gòkè. Fún ìkígbe (!), ohùn máa ń lágbára.

## Àwọn ìbéèrè ìmọ̀

1. Ọjọ́ wo ni ìyá àti ọmọ lọ sí ọjà? (Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta.)
2. Kí ni ìyá ra? (Iṣu méjì àti ata díẹ̀.)
3. Kí ló dé tí wọ́n fi dúró nínú ilé ìtajà? (Nítorí òjò bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí rọ̀.)

## Ìdánrawò kíkà

- Ka ìpín kọ̀ọ̀kan lẹ́ẹ̀mẹta.
- Bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́ra, lẹ́yìn náà yára díẹ̀.
- Tẹ́tí sí ara rẹ tàbí sí ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ.
- Samisi ọ̀rọ̀ tí ohùn rẹ̀ nira fún ọ.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Kíkà sókè dára nígbà tí ohùn ọ̀rọ̀ bá tọ́, tí a dúró níbi àmì ìdánudúró, tí a kò yára jù, tí a sì fi ìmọ̀lára hàn.

6.topic: Èrò pàtàkì àti àlàyé nínú ìpín ìwé (Main ideas and supporting details)
6.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. read a short Yoruba passage and state its main idea in one sentence;
2. pick out details from the passage that support the main idea;
3. give an opinion about the passage and support it with a reason from the text.

## Materials

The passage "Bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ àgbẹ̀" on a chart, highlighters or coloured chalk, sentence strips, notebooks.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: if you had to tell a friend what a story is about in one sentence, what would you say? Take two or three answers on a story pupils know and note which are too small (one detail) and which are right.

## Development

1. Define èrò pàtàkì (main idea) as what the passage is mostly about, and àlàyé (supporting detail) as the facts or examples that explain or support it.
2. Read the passage aloud. Ask pupils in Yoruba: Kí ni ìpín yìí dá lé lórí? (What is the passage about?)
3. Show how to find the main idea: read the first and last sentences, look for the idea that most of the passage supports, and avoid choosing a detail.
4. List the details on the board: ohun tí bàbá ń gbin, àkókò tí ó dìde, ohun tí ìyá ń tà, ohun tí Tọ́pẹ́ ń ṣe ní ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta.
5. Show a wrong choice: "Ìyá Tọ́pẹ́ ń tà ẹ̀fọ́" is a detail, not the main idea.
6. Pupils find the reason Tọ́pẹ́ likes farm work and say whether they agree that farming is important.

## Class activity

In pairs, pupils choose a different passage from a short set on cards. They underline the main idea once and each supporting detail twice. They present to another pair.

## Evaluation

1. What is the main idea of the passage?
2. Name two supporting details.
3. Why is a detail not a main idea?

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ àgbẹ̀
reading.content:
# Bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ àgbẹ̀

Bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ jẹ́ àgbẹ̀. Ó ní oko ńlá kan ní ẹ̀bá Ọ̀yọ́. Ní oko náà, ó ń gbin àgbàdo, iṣu àti ẹ̀fọ́.

Ní àárọ̀, bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ máa ń dìde ní aago márùn-ún láti lọ sí oko. Ìyá Tọ́pẹ́ máa ń tà ẹ̀fọ́ ní ọjà ní ọjọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan.

Ní ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, Tọ́pẹ́ máa ń bá bàbá rẹ̀ ṣiṣẹ́ ní oko. Ó fẹ́ràn iṣẹ́ oko nítorí ó ń jẹ́ kí ó mọ bí oúnjẹ ṣe ń wá. Bàbá rẹ̀ sọ pé iṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì nítorí pé láì sí àgbẹ̀, ebi yóò pa gbogbo ènìyàn.

## Èrò pàtàkì àti àlàyé

**Èrò pàtàkì (main idea)** ni ohun tí ìpín ìwé náà dá lé lórí jù. A lè sọ ọ́ ní gbólóhùn kan.

**Àlàyé (supporting details)** ni àwọn òtítọ́ tàbí àpẹẹrẹ tí ó ṣàlàyé tàbí tí ó tì èrò pàtàkì lẹ́yìn.

### Àpẹẹrẹ láti inú ìpín náà

Èrò pàtàkì: **Iṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì.**

Àwọn àlàyé:

1. Bàbá Tọ́pẹ́ ń gbin àgbàdo, iṣu àti ẹ̀fọ́.
2. Ìyá Tọ́pẹ́ ń tà ẹ̀fọ́ ní ọjà.
3. Tọ́pẹ́ fẹ́ràn iṣẹ́ oko nítorí ó ń kọ́ ọ bí oúnjẹ ṣe ń wá.
4. Láì sí àgbẹ̀, ebi yóò pa gbogbo ènìyàn.

## Bí a ṣe lè rí èrò pàtàkì

1. Ka gbogbo ìpín náà.
2. Béèrè pé: "Kí ni ìpín yìí dá lé lórí jù?"
3. Wo gbólóhùn àkọ́kọ́ àti gbólóhùn ìkẹyìn.
4. Yan èrò tí ọ̀pọ̀ gbólóhùn ń tì lẹ́yìn.
5. Má ṣe yan àlàyé kan ṣoṣo gẹ́gẹ́ bí èrò pàtàkì. "Ìyá Tọ́pẹ́ ń tà ẹ̀fọ́" jẹ́ àlàyé, kì í ṣe èrò pàtàkì.

## Ìdáhùn pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rí

Bí a bá béèrè èrò rẹ, sọ èrò rẹ, lẹ́yìn náà sọ ìdí rẹ̀ láti inú ìpín náà.

Àpẹẹrẹ: Mo gbà pé iṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀ ṣe pàtàkì nítorí pé ìpín náà sọ pé láì sí àgbẹ̀, ebi yóò pa gbogbo ènìyàn.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Èrò pàtàkì jẹ́ ohun tí ìpín ìwé dá lé jù. Àlàyé ń tì í lẹ́yìn.

8.topic: Àkọsílẹ̀ kúkúrú: àpèjúwe àti ìtàn (Short compositions: description and narrative)
8.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. write a short descriptive composition with a title, a beginning, a middle and an ending;
2. write a short narrative that presents events in order using linking words (ní àkọ́kọ́, lẹ́yìn náà, nígbẹ̀yìn);
3. check their work for complete sentences, correct tone marks and under-dots.

## Materials

A model composition on a chart, a chart of linking words, pictures of a school compound and of a rainy road, notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask pupils to say in Yoruba what they did first, next and last this morning before school. Write three sentences using ní àkọ́kọ́, lẹ́yìn náà and nígbẹ̀yìn.

## Development

1. Revise the three parts of a composition: ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ (beginning, introduce the subject), àárín (middle, give details or events) and ìparí (ending, close and give a final thought).
2. Descriptive writing. Show the model "Ilé Ìwé Mi". Underline the adjectives (ńlá, tóbi, onínúure) and the sentence that gives an opinion at the end.
3. Narrative writing. Show how to write events in order: who, when, what happened first, next, last. Use the linking words ní àkọ́kọ́ (at first), lẹ́yìn náà (after that), nígbà tí (when) and nígbẹ̀yìn (finally).
4. Plan together on the board: a spider diagram for the description and a time line for the narrative.
5. Pupils write their first draft in ten minutes, then read it aloud to a partner.
6. Check list for pupils: Does it have a title? Are the sentences complete? Are the marks correct? Does it end well?

## Class activity

Swap and mark. Pupils exchange drafts and put a tick for each correct point on the check list. They write one kind comment in Yoruba, such as "Ó dára, ṣùgbọ́n fi àmì ohùn sí i".

## Evaluation

1. What are the three parts of a composition?
2. Which linking words tell us that events are in order?
3. Write a closing sentence for "Ilé Ìwé Mi".

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Bí a ṣe ń kọ àkọsílẹ̀ kúkúrú

Àkọsílẹ̀ ni àyẹ̀wò tí a kọ nípa ohun kan. Àkọsílẹ̀ rere ní àkọlé àti apá mẹ́ta: **ìbẹ̀rẹ̀**, **àárín** àti **ìparí**.

## 1. Àkọsílẹ̀ àpèjúwe

Àkọsílẹ̀ àpèjúwe ń sọ bí ènìyàn, ibi tàbí nǹkan ṣe rí.

### Àpẹẹrẹ

**Ilé Ìwé Mi**

Ilé ìwé mi wà ní Ìbàdàn, ní ẹ̀bá ọjà. Ilé ìwé wa tóbi, ó sì ní pápá ìṣeré ńlá. Ní àárọ̀, a máa ń pé jọ fún ìpàdé àárọ̀. Lẹ́yìn náà, a máa ń lọ sí kíláàsì wa. Mo fẹ́ràn ilé ìwé mi nítorí àwọn olùkọ́ wa jẹ́ onínúure.

- **Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀:** sọ ohun tí a ń ṣàpèjúwe (orúkọ àti ibi).
- **Àárín:** sọ àwọn àlàyé (tóbi, pápá ìṣeré, ìpàdé àárọ̀).
- **Ìparí:** sọ èrò rẹ (Mo fẹ́ràn ilé ìwé mi nítorí ...).

## 2. Àkọsílẹ̀ ìtàn

Àkọsílẹ̀ ìtàn ń sọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ìlànà.

### Àpẹẹrẹ

**Ọjọ́ tí òjò rọ̀**

Ní ọjọ́ kan, mo ń lọ sí ilé ìwé. Ní àkọ́kọ́, ojú ọ̀run kún fún ìkùukùu. Lẹ́yìn náà, òjò ńlá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí rọ̀. Mo sá wọ abẹ́ igi kan. Nígbẹ̀yìn, òjò dá, mo sì dé ilé ìwé pẹ́ díẹ̀.

## Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀ tí ó wúlò

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| ní àkọ́kọ́ | at first, first of all |
| lẹ́yìn náà | after that |
| nígbà tí | when |
| nígbẹ̀yìn | finally, in the end |
| nítorí náà | therefore |

## Bí a ṣe ń ṣètò àkọsílẹ̀

1. Yan àkọlé.
2. Ronú nípa ohun tí o fẹ́ sọ: kọ ọ̀rọ̀ díẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
3. Kọ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, àárín àti ìparí.
4. Ka a padà. Ṣàtúnṣe àmì ohùn àti ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀.
5. Rí i dájú pé gbólóhùn kọ̀ọ̀kan kún.

## Àwọn àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

- Kíkọ gbólóhùn kan ṣoṣo àti pípe é àkọsílẹ̀.
- Àìlo ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀, tí ó mú kí ìtàn dà rú.
- Kíkọ ìparí tí kò bá àkọsílẹ̀ mu.
- Àìkọ àmì ohùn.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Àkọsílẹ̀ rere ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, àárín àti ìparí. Ìtàn gbọdọ̀ tẹ̀lé ìlànà àkókò.

9.topic: Ọ̀rọ̀ àdúgbò: ilé, ilé ìwé, àgbègbè àti àyíká (Vocabulary: home, school, community and environment)
9.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. name common things in the home, the school, the community and the environment in Yoruba;
2. use the new words correctly in short sentences with their tone marks and under-dots;
3. sort words into groups by topic.

## Materials

Picture cards or real objects (a chair, a pencil, a leaf, a toy bus), four labelled baskets (Ilé, Ilé ìwé, Àgbègbè, Àyíká), chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Hold up a picture of a classroom. Pupils name as many things in it as they can in Yoruba. Write the words they know and highlight the ones they do not know.

## Development

1. Teach each group with pictures. Home (ilé): yàrá (room), àga (chair), tábìlì (table), ilẹ̀kùn (door), fèrèsé (window), ilé ìdáná (kitchen), àgbàlá (yard), ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ (toilet).
2. School (ilé ìwé): akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ (pupil), olùkọ́ (teacher), kíláàsì (class), ìwé (book), pẹ́ńsùlù (pencil), pátákó (board).
3. Community (àgbègbè): ọjà (market), ilé ìwòsàn (hospital), ṣọ́ọ̀ṣì (church), mọ́sálásí (mosque), ọlọ́pàá (police officer), ibùdókọ̀ (bus stop), ọ̀nà (road), odò (river).
4. Environment (àyíká): igi (tree), ewé (leaf), òjò (rain), oòrùn (sun), ẹ̀fúùfù (wind), ẹranko (animal), ẹyẹ (bird), odò (river).
5. Practise saying each word aloud. Tap the syllables.
6. Pupils write one sentence for each group using one new word each time.

## Class activity

Basket game. The teacher holds up a card and says the Yoruba word. The first pupil to place the card in the right basket and say a sentence with it scores a point for the group.

## Evaluation

1. Name three things in a kitchen or a living room in Yoruba.
2. What is a hospital in Yoruba?
3. Write a sentence using the word "igi".

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

Bí a bá ní ọ̀rọ̀ púpọ̀ ní Yorùbá, a lè sọ̀rọ̀ nípa gbogbo ohun tí ó yí wa ká. Ẹ jẹ́ kí a kọ́ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tuntun ní ẹ̀ka mẹ́rin.

## 1. Ní ilé (At home)

10.topic: Lẹ́tà àìgbọ́dọ̀, ìránṣẹ́ àti àkọsílẹ̀ kúkúrú (Informal letters, messages and notes)
10.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. write a short informal letter in Yoruba with an address, a date, a greeting, a body and a closing;
2. write a short message or note that gives the essential information;
3. choose the right form of address (yín for elders, rẹ for friends) in a letter.

## Materials

A sample letter on a chart with the parts labelled, sample notes pinned up, letter paper or notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: when did you last leave a note for someone at home? What did you say? Take two or three. Point out that a good note says where you are, when you will return and why.

## Development

1. Show the parts of an informal letter: the writer's address and the date at the top right, the greeting (Bàbá mi ọ̀wọ́n, Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n), the body in short paragraphs, and the closing with the writer's name (Ọmọ yín, Ayọ̀; Ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ, Tọ́pẹ́).
2. Teach the opening phrases: Mo kí yín (I greet you), Mo nírètí pé ẹ wà dáadáa (I hope you are well). For a friend: Mo kí ọ, Mo nírètí pé o wà dáadáa.
3. Point out the forms of address: ẹ and yín for parents, grandparents and teachers; o and rẹ for friends and younger people.
4. Teach the note: no address or long greeting is needed. Give the message, the time and the sign-off: Mo ti lọ sí ọjà. N óò dé ní aago mẹ́fà.
5. Teach useful words: ọjọ́ ìbí (birthday), ayẹyẹ (party), pè (invite), wá (come), dé (arrive), iṣẹ́ àṣetiléwá (homework).
6. Pupils draft a letter and a note, then swap with a partner for checking.

## Class activity

Post box. Each pupil writes a note to a classmate and drops it into a box. The teacher hands the notes out. The reader says if the note tells where, when and why.

## Evaluation

1. How do you start a letter to your father?
2. Where do you write the date in an informal letter?
3. Write a two-line note telling your mother you have gone to the market.

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Lẹ́tà àti ìránṣẹ́ ní èdè Yorùbá
reading.content:
# Lẹ́tà àti ìránṣẹ́ ní èdè Yorùbá

Lẹ́tà jẹ́ ọ̀nà tí a fi ń bá ẹni tí ó jìnnà sọ̀rọ̀. Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú sì jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ díẹ̀ tí a fi sílẹ̀ fún ẹnìkan nílé tàbí ní ilé ìwé. Bí a ṣe ń kọ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan yàtọ̀.

## Lẹ́tà àìgbọ́dọ̀ (informal letter)

A máa ń kọ lẹ́tà àìgbọ́dọ̀ sí ẹbí tàbí ọ̀rẹ́. Ó ní apá márùn-ún:

1. **Adirẹ́ẹ̀sì ẹni tí ó kọ̀wé.** A kọ ọ́ sí òkè, ní apá ọ̀tún.
2. **Déètì.** A kọ ọ́ lábẹ́ adirẹ́ẹ̀sì.
3. **Ìkíni ìbẹ̀rẹ̀.** Bàbá mi ọ̀wọ́n, Ìyá mi ọ̀wọ́n, Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n.
4. **Ara lẹ́tà.** Ìpín kúkúrú kan tàbí méjì.
5. **Ìparí.** Ọmọ yín, Ayọ̀. Ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ, Tọ́pẹ́.

### Àpẹẹrẹ lẹ́tà sí ọ̀rẹ́

Ìbàdàn.
Ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà.

Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n,

Mo kí ọ. Mo nírètí pé o wà dáadáa. Ọjọ́ ìbí mi ni ní Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, aago mẹ́ta ọ̀sán, ní ilé wa. Mo fẹ́ kí o wá.

Ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ,
Ayọ̀.

### Àpẹẹrẹ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ lẹ́tà sí òbí

Bàbá mi ọ̀wọ́n,

Mo kí yín. Mo nírètí pé ẹ wà dáadáa. Èmi wà dáadáa ní ilé ìwé.

Ọmọ yín,
Tọ́pẹ́.

## Ìyàtọ̀ nínú bí a ṣe ń sọ̀rọ̀

- Fún àgbà tàbí òbí: **ẹ** àti **yín** (Mo kí yín, ẹ wà dáadáa).
- Fún ọ̀rẹ́ tàbí ẹni tí ó kéré: **o** àti **rẹ** (Mo kí ọ, o wà dáadáa).

## Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú (message or note)

Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú kò nílò adirẹ́ẹ̀sì tàbí ìkíni gígùn. Ó gbọdọ̀ sọ:

1. ibi tí a wà tàbí tí a lọ;
2. àkókò tí a óò dé;
3. ìdí, bí ó bá yẹ;
4. orúkọ ẹni tí ó kọ ọ́.

### Àpẹẹrẹ

Ìyá mi, mo ti lọ sí ilé ọ̀rẹ́ mi láti ṣe iṣẹ́ àṣetiléwá. N óò dé ní aago mẹ́fà ìrọ̀lẹ́.
Ọmọ yín, Ayọ̀.

## Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó wúlò

- ọjọ́ ìbí: birthday
- ayẹyẹ: party, celebration
- pè: to invite, to call
- wá: to come
- dé: to arrive
- iṣẹ́ àṣetiléwá: homework

## Àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

1. Lílo "rẹ" fún àgbà (ó yẹ kí a lo "yín").
2. Gbígbàgbé orúkọ ẹni tí ó kọ ọ́ ní ìparí.
3. Kíkọ ìránṣẹ́ láì sọ àkókò.
4. Àìkọ àmì ohùn.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Lẹ́tà ní apá márùn-ún. Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú gbọdọ̀ sọ ibi, àkókò àti orúkọ.
